

```{r Initialise}
##setwd()

#######################r initialization####################
# Clear workspace
rm(list=ls()) 

# Load libraries
# Install required packages if not already installed
library(readr)        # For reading CSV files
library(tidyverse)    # For data manipulation and plotting
library(sf)           # For reading and handling spatial data
library(spdep)        # For spatial analysis, including Getis-Ord Gi*
library(tmap)         # For thematic mapping
library(lubridate)    # For date manipulation
library(kableExtra)   # For table formatting
library(dplyr)         # For data manipulation
library(terra)
library(geodata)
library(traveltime)
library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyterra)

# Source to current directory and set working directory
basePath <- getwd()

# Restart R and set working directory to source file location. 

##r User inputs
##select project
selectedproject<- "late_hiv_diagnosis"

# Various directories
projectFolder <- file.path(basePath,"projects", selectedproject)
dataFolder <- file.path(basePath,"projects", selectedproject,"data")
resultsFolder <- file.path(basePath,"projects", selectedproject, "output")
figFolder <- file.path(basePath,"projects", selectedproject,"figures")
# HIV data folder - for sourcing latest notification cleaning files
HIVDataFolder <- file.path("C:", "onedrive", "OneDrive - UNSW", "HIV Trends Across Space and Time", 
  "General")
```

```{r Input}
# Specify project input files and load them
hivdataFile<- file.path(HIVDataFolder, "hiv_data_cleaned_20250731.csv")
# Read the CSV data
hiv_data_all <- read_csv(hivdataFile, col_types = cols(
  month_hiv_diag = col_character(),
  age_hiv_notif = col_double(),
  sex = col_character(),
  gender = col_character(),
  region_birth = col_character(),
  au_birth = col_character(),
  lang_home = col_character(),
  year_arrival_aus = col_double(),
  cd4_count_diag = col_double(),
  late_hiv_diag_flag = col_logical(), 
  newly_acq_hiv_flag = col_logical(),
  hiv_exposure_risk = col_character(),
  place_acq = col_character(),
  state_res = col_character(),
  phn_res = col_character(),
  phn_name = col_character(),
  previ_diag_overseas = col_logical(),
  id = col_double(),
  year_diag = col_double()
))

hiv_data_all <- hiv_data_all %>%
  mutate(
    advanced_hiv_diag_flag = case_when(
      # If late_hiv_diag_flag is NA, return NA
      is.na(late_hiv_diag_flag) ~ NA,
      # If both conditions are met (cd4 < 200 AND late diagnosis), return TRUE
      cd4_count_diag < 200 & late_hiv_diag_flag == TRUE ~ TRUE,
      # All other cases return FALSE
      TRUE ~ FALSE
    )
  )

hiv_data_all <- hiv_data_all %>%
  mutate(
    cd4_50_hiv_diag_flag = case_when(
      # If late_hiv_diag_flag is NA, return NA
      is.na(late_hiv_diag_flag) ~ NA,
      # If both conditions are met (cd4 < 50 AND late diagnosis), return TRUE
      cd4_count_diag < 50 & late_hiv_diag_flag == TRUE ~ TRUE,
      # All other cases return FALSE
      TRUE ~ FALSE
    )
  )

hiv_data <- hiv_data_all %>%
  filter(
    is.na(age_hiv_notif) | age_hiv_notif >= 18
  )

# Check data structure
str(hiv_data)

# Read PHN shapefile
shapefile_path <- file.path(dataFolder, "phn.shp")
phn_shp <- st_read(shapefile_path)

# Inspect shapefile attribute fields
names(phn_shp)

# Ensure phn_res matches the PHN shapefile ID
# Suppose PHN shapefile has a column named "PHN_CODE"
phn_data <- phn_shp %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::select(PHN_CODE) # Adjust as needed

# Check matching PHNs
unique(hiv_data$phn_res)
unique(phn_data$PHN_CODE)

# Load Australia shapefile for masking
au_shapefile <- gadm(
 country = "Australia",
 level = 0,
 path = tempdir(),
 resolution = 2
 )
au_shapefile


# Define location dataset file paths
s100File   <- file.path(dataFolder, "s100_20250711.xlsx")
gp_path    <- file.path(dataFolder, "nhsd_general_practice_full_20250819.xlsx")
hosp_path  <- file.path(dataFolder, "nhsd_hospitals_full_20250819.xlsx")
shc_path   <- file.path(dataFolder, "public_sexual_health_clinics_20250818.xlsx")

# Process S100 data
s100_data <- read_excel(s100File) %>%
  filter(label %in% c(0, 4)) %>%  # Only keep label = 0 or 4 to avoid duplicates
  select(x, y) %>%
  filter(!is.na(x), !is.na(y)) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(
    s100_label = 1,              # All S100 locations get s100_label = 1
    type = "others100"           # Type is "others100"
  )

# Process GP data
gp_data <- read_excel(gp_path) %>%
  filter(is.na(sexual_clinic) |sexual_clinic == 1) %>%     # Exclude sexual clinics to avoid duplicates with shc_path
  select(lon_final, lat_final, s100_label) %>%
  rename(x = lon_final, y = lat_final) %>%
  filter(!is.na(x), !is.na(y)) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(
    s100_label = case_when(
      s100_label == 1 ~ 1,
      is.na(s100_label) ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    type = "gp"
  )

# Process Hospital data
hosp_data <- read_excel(hosp_path) %>%
  filter(is.na(sexual_clinic) |sexual_clinic != 1) %>%     # Exclude sexual clinics to avoid duplicates with shc_path
  select(lon_final, lat_final, s100_label) %>%
  rename(x = lon_final, y = lat_final) %>%
  filter(!is.na(x), !is.na(y)) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(
    s100_label = case_when(
      s100_label == 1 ~ 1,
      is.na(s100_label) ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    type = "hospital"
  )

# Process Sexual Health Clinics data
shc_data <- read_excel(shc_path) %>%
  filter(!is.na(x), !is.na(y), free %in% c(1,2,5) ) %>% # add filter for free clinics only
  select(x, y, s100_label) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(
    s100_label = case_when(
      s100_label == 1 ~ 1,
      is.na(s100_label) ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    type = "shc"
  )

# Combine all datasets
location_combined_data <- bind_rows(
  s100_data,
  gp_data,
  hosp_data,
  shc_data
) %>%
  select(x, y, s100_label, type) %>%
  distinct()  # Remove any remaining duplicates
```

```{r Travel time calculation}
#### Jump this if loaded ####

# Select locations for travel time calculation
selected_location_full <- location_combined_data 

selected_location_full <- location_combined_data %>%
                           filter(type == "shc")

selected_location <- selected_location_full %>%
                     select(x, y)

# 1. Get friction surface for Australia and mask to country boundary
friction_au <- get_friction_surface(
    surface = "motor2020",
    extent = au_shapefile
  )|> 
  mask(au_shapefile)


selected_location_sf <- st_as_sf(selected_location, coords = c("x","y"), crs = 4326)

# 2. Inspect the friction raster’s CRS and extent
crs(friction_au)        # e.g. "+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84…"
ext(rast(friction_au))  # get its bounding box

# 3. Reproject points to match
selected_location_proj <- st_transform(selected_location_sf, crs(friction_au))

# 4. filter to only those within the raster’s extent
bb <- ext(rast(friction_au))
coords <- st_coordinates(selected_location_proj)
inside <- coords[,1] >= bb$xmin & coords[,1] <= bb$xmax &
          coords[,2] >= bb$ymin & coords[,2] <= bb$ymax
selected_location_clean <- coords[inside, , drop=FALSE]
selected_location_sf_clean <- selected_location_proj[inside, , drop = FALSE]
selected_location_full_clean <- selected_location_full[inside, ]

# 5. Run travel time
travel_time_au <- calculate_travel_time(
  friction_surface = friction_au,
  points           = selected_location_clean
)

#### save the rasters ####
cacheFolder <- file.path(dataFolder, "_cache")

fric_file <- file.path(cacheFolder, "friction_motor2020_au_freeshc.tif")
tt_file   <- file.path(cacheFolder, "traveltime_au_motor2020_pointsset_v1_freeshc.tif")
pts_file  <- file.path(cacheFolder, "points_used_for_traveltime_freeshc.csv")
meta_file <- file.path(cacheFolder, "traveltime_au_metadata_freeshc.json")

# Write friction raster only if not already present
if (!file.exists(fric_file)) {
  terra::writeRaster(
    friction_au, fric_file,
    overwrite = FALSE,
    gdal = c("TILED=YES", "COMPRESS=LZW", "BIGTIFF=YES")
  )
} else {
  message("File already exists: ", fric_file)
}

# Write points CSV only if not already present
if (!file.exists(pts_file)) {
  readr::write_csv(as.data.frame(selected_location_full_clean), pts_file)
} else {
  message("File already exists: ", pts_file)
}

# Write travel time raster only if not already present
if (!file.exists(tt_file)) {
  terra::writeRaster(
    travel_time_au, tt_file,
    overwrite = FALSE,
    datatype = "FLT4S",
    NAflag = -9999,
    gdal = c("TILED=YES", "COMPRESS=LZW", "BIGTIFF=YES")
  )
} else {
  message("File already exists: ", tt_file)
}

# Write metadata only if not already present
if (!file.exists(meta_file)) {
  meta <- list(
    created_at = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    surface = "motor2020",
    raster_file = tt_file,
    friction_file = fric_file,
    n_points = nrow(selected_location_clean),
    crs_wkt = as.character(terra::crs(travel_time_au))
  )
  jsonlite::write_json(meta, meta_file, pretty = TRUE, auto_unbox = TRUE)
} else {
  message("File already exists: ", meta_file)
}


#### Travel time of PHN based on 2024 population grid ~1km ####
# 1-km ABS population grid (density: people per km^2)
pop_grid <- terra::rast(file.path(dataFolder, "abs_popgrid_1km_2024.tif"))

# Source (counts/cell) -> density (people/km^2) on the *source* grid
area_src <- terra::cellSize(pop_grid, unit = "km")
dens_src <- pop_grid / area_src

# Project density to the *target* 
# Make sure travel_time_au has a valid CRS first:
terra::crs(travel_time_au) <- terra::crs(friction_au)
dens_tgt <- terra::project(dens_src, travel_time_au, method = "bilinear")

# Convert density back to counts on the *target* grid
area_tgt <- terra::cellSize(travel_time_au, unit = "km")
pop_count_res <- dens_tgt * area_tgt

# Mask to Australia
pop_count_res <- terra::mask(pop_count_res, au_shapefile)

# Clean inputs
travel_time_au_clean <- terra::ifel(is.finite(travel_time_au), travel_time_au, NA)
pop_count_res        <- terra::ifel(is.finite(pop_count_res) & pop_count_res >= 0, pop_count_res, NA)

library(exactextractr)

# Stack so the reducer sees both layers
stack_tt_pop <- c(travel_time_au, pop_count_res)

phn_avg_reach <- exact_extract(
  x = stack_tt_pop,
  y = phn_shp,
  fun = function(df, cf) {
    # df[[1]] = travel time; df[[2]] = pop count per cell
    tt  <- df[[1]]
    pop <- df[[2]]

    keep <- is.finite(tt) & is.finite(pop) & (pop > 0) &
            is.finite(cf) & (cf > 0)

    if (!any(keep)) return(NA_real_)  # no reachable population -> NA
    sum(tt[keep] * pop[keep] * cf[keep]) / sum(pop[keep] * cf[keep])
  },
  progress = TRUE
)

phn_map_reach <- phn_shp |>
  dplyr::mutate(avg_drive_min_reach = phn_avg_reach)

library(sf)

phn_travel_file <- file.path(cacheFolder, "phn_travel_freeshc.gpkg")

if (!file.exists(phn_travel_file)) {
  sf::st_write(
    phn_map_reach,
    dsn = phn_travel_file,
    driver = "GPKG"
  )
  message("✅ Saved new file: ", phn_travel_file)
} else {
  message("⚠️ File already exists, skipping: ", phn_travel_file)
}


#### Extract travel time for all cells into data.frame ####
# This will give a data.frame with columns: x, y, travel_time
df_all_cells <- terra::as.data.frame(
  travel_time_au,
  xy     = TRUE,       # include coordinates
  na.rm  = FALSE       # keep cells with NA or Inf if you want
)
```

```{r Syd area travel time plotting}
#### SYD AREA - WITH BOUNDARY CLIPPING ####
# 1) Select PHN101–PHN105 and union
syd_codes <- paste0("PHN", 101:103)
syd_phn   <- phn_shp |> dplyr::filter(PHN_CODE %in% syd_codes)
syd_union <- sf::st_union(syd_phn)

# 1a) Keep only the MAINLAND component (largest polygon)
# Break into individual polygons
syd_components <- sf::st_cast(syd_union, "MULTIPOLYGON") |> sf::st_cast("POLYGON")

# Calculate area for each polygon
syd_components$area <- sf::st_area(syd_components)

# Keep the two largest polygons
syd_mainland <- syd_components[order(syd_components$area, decreasing = TRUE)[1:2], ] |>
  sf::st_make_valid()

# Union them back into one geometry
syd_mainland <- sf::st_union(syd_mainland) |> sf::st_make_valid()

pad_dist_m <- 25000
metric_crs <- 3577                     # GDA94 / Australia Albers (meters)
rast_crs   <- terra::crs(friction_au)  # WKT string is fine for st_transform

# Buffer 25 km in metric CRS, then transform to raster CRS
syd_buf_rast <- syd_mainland |>
  sf::st_transform(metric_crs) |>
  sf::st_buffer(pad_dist_m) |>
  sf::st_transform(rast_crs) |>
  sf::st_make_valid()

# Build bbox in the **raster CRS**
syd_bbox <- sf::st_bbox(syd_buf_rast)
syd_ext  <- terra::ext(c(syd_bbox$xmin, syd_bbox$xmax, syd_bbox$ymin, syd_bbox$ymax))

# Convert the mainland polygon to SpatVector in the **raster CRS** for masking
syd_mask_sv <- terra::vect(sf::st_transform(syd_mainland, rast_crs))

# Crop + mask (now CRS-aligned, warning disappears)
friction_syd <- friction_au |>
  terra::crop(syd_ext) |>
  terra::mask(syd_mask_sv)

syd_bbox_crs <- syd_bbox

# 4) Filter prescribers to be strictly within PHN boundaries (keep attributes)
# IMPORTANT: selected_location_full_clean was saved in the raster CRS earlier.
pts_full_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(
  selected_location_full_clean,
  coords = c("x","y"),
  crs    = terra::crs(friction_au),  
  remove = FALSE
)

# Make sure Sydney PHNs are in the same CRS
syd_phn_rast <- sf::st_transform(syd_phn, terra::crs(friction_au))

# Keep only points within Sydney PHNs
pts_sf_syd <- sf::st_filter(pts_full_sf, syd_phn_rast, .predicate = sf::st_intersects)

# Create a plain data.frame with x/y in raster CRS + attributes (like *_full_clean)
coords_syd <- sf::st_coordinates(pts_sf_syd)
selected_location_full_syd <- pts_sf_syd |>
  dplyr::mutate(x = coords_syd[,1], y = coords_syd[,2]) |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  dplyr::select(x, y, s100_label, type) |>
  dplyr::distinct()

selected_location_syd <- pts_sf_syd

library(ggnewscale)
library(ggplot2)

# Build Sydney pop=0 mask and TT masked to pop>0
pop_count_res_syd <- pop_count_res |>
  terra::crop(friction_syd) |>
  terra::mask(syd_mask_sv)

pop_zero_mask_syd <- terra::ifel(pop_count_res_syd == 0, 1, NA)
tt_nonzero_syd    <- terra::mask(travel_time_syd, pop_zero_mask_syd, maskvalues = 1)

#### PLOT Sydney travel time with prescribers ####
tt_syd_plot <- ggplot() +
  # Grey background for zero-pop cells
  tidyterra::geom_spatraster(data = pop_zero_mask_syd) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = c("grey85","grey85"),
    limits  = c(0, 1),
    breaks  = 1,
    labels  = "Population = 0",
    na.value = NA,
    name    = NULL
  ) +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +

  # Travel time only where pop > 0
  tidyterra::geom_spatraster(data = tt_nonzero_syd) +
  # Color scale for travel time
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = rev(rainbow(4)),
    limits  = c(0, 60),
    oob     = scales::squish,
    breaks  = c(0, 30, 60),
    labels  = c("0", "30", ">60"),
    na.value = "transparent"
  ) +

  # Prescriber points (Sydney-only), colored by S100 status
  geom_point(
    data = selected_location_full_syd |>

#### SYD AREA ####
# 1) Select PHN101–PHN105 and union
syd_codes <- paste0("PHN", 101:103)
syd_phn   <- phn_shp |> dplyr::filter(PHN_CODE %in% syd_codes)
syd_union <- sf::st_union(syd_phn)

# 1a) Keep only the MAINLAND component (largest polygon)
# Break into individual polygons
syd_components <- sf::st_cast(syd_union, "MULTIPOLYGON") |> sf::st_cast("POLYGON")

# Calculate area for each polygon
syd_components$area <- sf::st_area(syd_components)

# Keep the two largest polygons
syd_mainland <- syd_components[order(syd_components$area, decreasing = TRUE)[1:2], ] |>
  sf::st_make_valid()

# Union them back into one geometry
syd_mainland <- sf::st_union(syd_mainland)

# 2) Build a padded bbox from the mainland only (CRS‑safe)
rcrs <- sf::st_crs(phn_shp)   # same as friction_au
pad_dist_m <- 25000
if (!is.na(rcrs$units_gdal) && rcrs$units_gdal == "metre") {
  bb_geom <- sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(syd_mainland))
  bb_pad  <- sf::st_buffer(bb_geom, dist = pad_dist_m)
  syd_bbox_crs <- sf::st_bbox(bb_pad)
} else {
  bb_geom <- sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(syd_mainland))
  bb_3857 <- sf::st_transform(bb_geom, 3857)
  bb_pad  <- sf::st_buffer(bb_3857, dist = pad_dist_m)
  bb_back <- sf::st_transform(bb_pad, rcrs)
  syd_bbox_crs <- sf::st_bbox(bb_back)
}

# 3) Crop/mask using the MAINLAND (no far‑away island)
syd_ext <- terra::ext(c(syd_bbox_crs$xmin, syd_bbox_crs$xmax,
                        syd_bbox_crs$ymin, syd_bbox_crs$ymax))
friction_syd <- terra::crop(friction_au, syd_ext) |>
  terra::mask(terra::vect(syd_mainland))

# 4) Filter points and recompute travel time (same as before, but bbox from mainland)
selected_location_sf   <- sf::st_as_sf(selected_location, coords = c("x","y"), crs = 4326) |> sf::st_transform(rcrs)
coords    <- sf::st_coordinates(selected_location_sf)
inside    <- coords[,1] >= syd_bbox_crs$xmin & coords[,1] <= syd_bbox_crs$xmax &
             coords[,2] >= syd_bbox_crs$ymin & coords[,2] <= syd_bbox_crs$ymax
selected_location_syd  <- selected_location_sf[inside, ]

travel_time_syd <- calculate_travel_time(
  friction_surface = friction_syd,
  points           = sf::st_coordinates(selected_location_syd)
) 

# 5) Plot, using syd_phn outlines but the mainland bbox
friction_syd_plot <- ggplot() +
  tidyterra::geom_spatraster(data = friction_syd) +
  tidyterra::geom_spatvector(data = terra::vect(syd_phn), fill = "transparent", col = "grey30") +
  tidyterra::geom_spatvector(data = selected_location_syd, col = "grey40", size = 0.5) +

#### Extracting mean travel time by SA2 ####
sa2_shapefile <- file.path(dataFolder, "SA2_2021_AUST_GDA94.shp")
sa2 <- st_read(sa2_shapefile)

# Pull the CRS from original friction surface (which should be valid)
orig_crs <- crs(friction_au)

# Assign it to travel‐time raster
crs(travel_time_au) <- orig_crs

# Now project SA2 vector to that CRS
sa2_vect <- vect(sa2) 
sa2_vect <- project(sa2_vect, orig_crs)

# Transform with sf to WGS84
sa2_wgs84 <- st_transform(sa2, crs = 4326)

# Convert to terra
sa2_vect <- vect(sa2_wgs84)

# double-check they match:
stopifnot(crs(sa2_vect) == crs(travel_time_au))

travel_time_au_exNA <- terra::ifel(
  !is.finite(travel_time_au),  # test infinite / NaN
  NA,                           # if TRUE, set to NA
  travel_time_au                # else keep original
)

# Re-extract mean per SA2
tt_sa2   <- terra::extract(
  travel_time_au_exNA,
  sa2_vect,
  fun    = mean,
  na.rm  = TRUE
)

# Attach back and anything still non-finite becomes NA
sa2$mean_travel_time_min <- tt_sa2[ , "travel_time"]

library(ggplot2)
library(viridis)   # for scale_fill_viridis_c()

  ) +
  theme_minimal() +

#### Australia-wide density map ####
# Using the already loaded data:
# - sa2: sf with SA2_CODE21 geometry
# - travel_time_au: terra SpatRaster (1 km travel time for Australia)
# - friction_au: terra SpatRaster
# - pop_sa2: already loaded with SA2_CODE21 and pop_size

# 1) Compute SA2 density (people per km²) for all of Australia
sa2_den_au <- sa2 |>
  left_join(pop_sa2, by = "SA2_CODE21") |>
  mutate(
    area_km2 = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)) / 1e6,
    pop_km2 = if_else(area_km2 > 0, pop_size / area_km2, NA_real_)
  )

# 2) Reproject SA2 to raster CRS and rasterize density onto the 1 km grid
terra::crs(travel_time_au) <- terra::crs(friction_au)
sa2_den_v_au <- terra::vect(st_transform(sa2_den_au, crs(travel_time_au)))
den_rast_au <- terra::rasterize(
  sa2_den_v_au,
  travel_time_au,
  field = "pop_km2",
  touches = TRUE
)

# 3) Choose a threshold
thr_fixed_au <- 0.01  # people per km²

# 4) Build masks for low/high density areas
low_density_mask_au <- den_rast_au < thr_fixed_au
tt_high_density_au <- terra::ifel(low_density_mask_au, NA, travel_time_au)

# 5) Plot the Australia-wide density map

#### Calculate average travel time by PHN through the average travel time and population size of SA2####
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

# Read in two lookup tables
pop_sa2   <- read_csv(file.path(dataFolder,"SA2_pop_size_2021.csv") , col_types = cols(
  SA2_NAME21 = col_character(),
  SA2_CODE21 = col_character(),
  pop_size = col_double()))     # columns: SA2_CODE21, pop_size
phn_lookup <- read_csv(file.path(dataFolder,"phn_sa2.csv"), col_types = cols_only(
  SA2_NAME21 = col_character(),
  SA2_CODE21 = col_character(),
  PHN_CODE = col_character(),
  PHN_NAME = col_character(),
  RATIO_FROM_TO = col_double()))    # columns: SA2_CODE21, PHN_CODE, PHN_NAME, RATIO_FROM_TO

# Pull out travel times from sf:
tt_sa2 <- sa2 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%                   # keep attributes only
  select(SA2_CODE21, mean_travel_time_min) %>%
  filter(!is.na(mean_travel_time_min))     # drop any SA2 with no valid time

# Join everything, allocate population, compute weighted mean
phn_tt <- tt_sa2 %>%
  inner_join(pop_sa2,    by = "SA2_CODE21") %>%     # add pop_size
  inner_join(phn_lookup, by = "SA2_CODE21") %>%     # add PHN and ratio
  mutate(
    pop_alloc = pop_size * RATIO_FROM_TO,
    weighted_time = mean_travel_time_min * pop_alloc
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(PHN_CODE)) %>%   
  group_by(PHN_CODE, PHN_NAME) %>%
  summarise(
    total_pop    = sum(pop_alloc,    na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_drive_min = sum(weighted_time, na.rm = TRUE) / total_pop,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

phn_tt1 <- tt_sa2 %>%
  inner_join(pop_sa2,    by = "SA2_CODE21") %>%     # add pop_size
  inner_join(phn_lookup, by = "SA2_CODE21") %>%     # add PHN and ratio
  mutate(
    pop_alloc = pop_size * RATIO_FROM_TO,
    weighted_time = mean_travel_time_min * pop_alloc
  ) %>%
  group_by(PHN_CODE, PHN_NAME) %>%
  filter(!is.na(weighted_time)) %>%
  summarise(
    total_pop    = sum(pop_alloc,    na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_drive_min = sum(weighted_time, na.rm = TRUE) / total_pop,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

phn_tt

# Join computed averages to the PHN shapefile
phn_map <- phn_shp %>%
  left_join(phn_tt, by = "PHN_CODE")

# Plot with ggplot2
phn_traveltime_mapping <- ggplot(phn_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = avg_drive_min), 
          colour = "grey50", size = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option    = "A",
    direction = -1,
    na.value  = "transparent",
    name      = "Avg Drive Time\n(minutes)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title    = "Population-Weighted Mean Drive Time by PHN",
    subtitle = "Australia, based on SA2 allocations and 1 km friction raster",
    x        = NULL, 
    y        = NULL
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text      = element_blank(),
    panel.grid     = element_blank(),
    plot.title     = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle  = element_text(size = 10)
  )



library(sf)

#### Central Sydney density map####
## - sa2: sf with SA2_CODE21 geometry
## - travel_time_syd: terra SpatRaster (1 km travel time)
## - friction_syd: terra SpatRaster (same grid/crs as travel_time_syd)
## - pop_sa2: data.frame with SA2_CODE21, pop_size

# 1) Compute SA2 density (people per km²)
sa2_den <- sa2 |>
  left_join(pop_sa2, by = "SA2_CODE21") |>
  mutate(
    area_km2   = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)) / 1e6,
    pop_km2    = if_else(area_km2 > 0, pop_size / area_km2, NA_real_)
  )

# 2) Reproject SA2 to raster CRS and rasterize density onto the 1 km grid
terra::crs(travel_time_syd) <- terra::crs(friction_syd)
sa2_den_v  <- terra::vect(st_transform(sa2_den, crs(travel_time_syd)))
den_rast   <- terra::rasterize(
  sa2_den_v,
  travel_time_syd,
  field   = "pop_km2",
  touches = TRUE          # fill cells touched by polygons
)

# 3) Choose a threshold (option A: fixed; option B: quantile-based)
thr_fixed <- 10   # people per km²
thr_q10   <- terra::global(den_rast, fun = quantile, probs = 0.10, na.rm = TRUE)[1]

# 4) Build a mask of cells to KEEP (>= threshold) and apply it
keep_mask <- den_rast >= thr_fixed   # or use thr_q10
tt_syd_masked <- terra::ifel(keep_mask, travel_time_syd, NA)

# Build a factor raster for low/high density classification
low_density_mask <- den_rast < thr_fixed

# Create a travel-time raster for plotting with NA for low-density cells
tt_high_density <- terra::ifel(low_density_mask, NA, travel_time_syd)
```

```{r distance to nearest prescriber}
library(terra)

prescriber_sf <- selected_location_proj   
# prescriber_sf: an sf with prescriber locations
pres_rast <- rasterize(
  vect(prescriber_sf),      # convert sf → SpatVector
  friction_au,              # template raster
  field = 1,                # mark prescriber cells = 1
  background = NA
)


dist_m  <- distance(pres_rast)   # terra::distance measures metres by default
dist_km <- dist_m / 1000         # convert to kilometres
dist_km <- terra::ifel(!is.finite(dist_km), NA, dist_km)
dist_km_aus <- terra::crop(dist_km, au_shapefile)
dist_km_aus <- terra::mask(dist_km_aus, au_shapefile)

smallest_section_distance_mapping <- ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = dist_km_aus) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option    = "A",
    direction = -1,
    na.value  = "transparent",
    name      = "Distance (km)"
  ) +
  geom_spatvector(
    data = phn_shp,
    fill = "transparent",
    col  = "grey20"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(fill = "Distance (km)")


# assign CRS if needed
crs(dist_km_aus) <- crs(friction_au)

# extract mean distance per SA2
tt_sa2_dist <- terra::extract(
  dist_km_aus,

  fun   = mean,

)

  inner_join(pop_sa2,    by="SA2_CODE21") %>%

  filter(!is.na(PHN_CODE)) %>%
  mutate(
    pop_alloc     = pop_size * RATIO_FROM_TO,

  ) %>%
  group_by(PHN_CODE, PHN_NAME) %>%
  summarise(
    total_pop     = sum(pop_alloc, na.rm=TRUE),
```

```{r logistic regression}
      right  = FALSE

    )

# Fit one glm per variable and tidy the results
univ_results <- map_dfr(vars, function(v) {
  # build formula
  fml <- as.formula(paste0("late_hiv_diag_flag ~ ", v))
  
  # fit univariate model
  m <- glm(fml, data = hiv_data_logistic, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
  
  # tidy: exponentiate to OR, get 95% CI and p-value
  tidy(m, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    # keep only the predictor row (drop intercept)
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    # add a column for which variable this was
    mutate(variable = v) %>%
    # rename for clarity
    select(variable, term, OR = estimate, `2.5 %` = conf.low, `97.5 %` = conf.high, p.value)
})

# Extract coefficients and calculate odds ratios

# Exponentiate both the point estimates and the CIs

  OR      = coef(model),
  CI_low  = ci_logodds[,1],
  CI_high = ci_logodds[,2]
))

# 3. label and view

# OR in other group
library(broom)
library(msm)

vcov_mat <- vcov(model)
coefs <- coef(model)
results <- list()

for (lvl in levels(hiv_data_logistic$avg_travel_min_group_s100)[-1]) {
  main_term <- paste0("avg_travel_min_group_s100", lvl)
  inter_term <- paste0("au_birthOverseas:avg_travel_min_group_s100", lvl)
  contrast <- rep(0, length(coefs))
  contrast[which(names(coefs)==main_term)] <- 1
  contrast[which(names(coefs)==inter_term)] <- 1
  est <- sum(coefs * contrast)
  se  <- sqrt(t(contrast) %*% vcov_mat %*% contrast)
  ci  <- c(est - 1.96*se, est + 1.96*se)
  results[[lvl]] <- data.frame(
    travel_time = lvl,
    OR = exp(est),
    CI_low = exp(ci[1]),
    CI_high = exp(ci[2])
  )
}
do.call(rbind, results)

#### 2. Univariate ordinal logistic regression ####
# ---- Ensure outcome variable is ordered factor (run once) ----
hiv_data_logistic <- hiv_data_logistic %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    avg_travel_min_group_s100 = factor(
      avg_travel_min_group_s100,
      levels = c("<15", "15-<30", "30-<60", "60+"),
      ordered = TRUE
    )
  )

# ---- Univariate ordinal logistic regression (robust version) ----
library(purrr)

univ_results <- purrr::map_dfr(vars, function(v) {
  # Subset and remove missing values
  df <- hiv_data_logistic %>%
    dplyr::select(avg_travel_min_group_s100, !!rlang::sym(v)) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(avg_travel_min_group_s100), !is.na(!!rlang::sym(v)))

  # If too few observations, return NA row
  if (nrow(df) < 5) {
    return(tibble::tibble(
      variable   = v,
      term       = NA_character_,
      OR         = NA_real_,
      `2.5 %`    = NA_real_,
      `97.5 %`   = NA_real_,
      p.value    = NA_real_,
      n_used     = nrow(df),
      levels_used= NA_character_
    ))
  }

  # Convert predictor: keep numeric as is, convert logical/character to factor
  x <- df[[v]]
  if (!is.numeric(x)) x <- factor(x)

  # If only one level, return NA row
  if (is.factor(x) && nlevels(x) < 2) {
    return(tibble::tibble(
      variable   = v,
      term       = NA_character_,
      OR         = NA_real_,
      `2.5 %`    = NA_real_,
      `97.5 %`   = NA_real_,
      p.value    = NA_real_,
      n_used     = nrow(df),
      levels_used= paste0("levels=", nlevels(x))
    ))
  }

  # Construct temporary dataset for fitting
  fit_df <- tibble::tibble(
    y = df$avg_travel_min_group_s100,
    x = x
  )

  # Fit the model and extract results
  res <- tryCatch({
    m <- MASS::polr(y ~ x, data = fit_df, Hess = TRUE)

    summ <- summary(m)
    coefs <- summ$coefficients[, "Value"]
    ses   <- summ$coefficients[, "Std. Error"]
    tvals <- summ$coefficients[, "t value"]

    coef_names <- rownames(summ$coefficients)
    keep <- grepl("^x", coef_names)   # keep only predictor-related terms

    # If no match, fallback: keep the last rows (likely the predictor terms)
    if (!any(keep)) {
      k <- length(coefs)
      keep <- rep(FALSE, k)
      last_n <- if (is.factor(x)) max(1, nlevels(x) - 1) else 1
      keep[(k - last_n + 1):k] <- TRUE
    }

    coefs <- coefs[keep]
    ses   <- ses[keep]
    tvals <- tvals[keep]
    names_kept <- coef_names[keep]

    # Odds ratios and Wald CI
    OR  <- exp(coefs)
    LCL <- exp(coefs - 1.96 * ses)
    UCL <- exp(coefs + 1.96 * ses)

    # p-values
    pvs <- 2 * pnorm(abs(tvals), lower.tail = FALSE)

    # Term labels
    if (is.factor(x)) {
      # Remove "x" prefix added by model.matrix, then combine with variable name
      level_terms <- sub("^x", "", names_kept)
      term_readable <- paste0(v, ":", level_terms)
      levels_used <- paste(levels(x), collapse = " | ")
    } else {
      term_readable <- v
      levels_used <- NA_character_
    }

    tibble::tibble(
      variable    = v,
      term        = term_readable,
      OR          = as.numeric(OR),
      `2.5 %`     = as.numeric(LCL),
      `97.5 %`    = as.numeric(UCL),
      p.value     = as.numeric(pvs),
      n_used      = nrow(fit_df),
      levels_used = levels_used
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    tibble::tibble(
      variable   = v,
      term       = NA_character_,
      OR         = NA_real_,
      `2.5 %`    = NA_real_,
      `97.5 %`   = NA_real_,
      p.value    = NA_real_,
      n_used     = nrow(df),
      levels_used= NA_character_
    )
  })

  res
})

# View results
print(univ_results)


#### 3. Multivariate ordinal logistic regression ####
# ---- 0) Ensure ordered outcome (run once) ----
hiv_data_logistic <- hiv_data_logistic %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    avg_travel_min_group_s100 = factor(
      avg_travel_min_group_s100,
      levels = c("<15", "15-<30", "30-<60", "60+"),
      ordered = TRUE
    )
  )

# ---- 1) Define predictors and make sure categoricals are factors with sensible baselines ----
preds <- c("hiv_exposure_risk_group", "sex", "au_birth", "age_group", "late_hiv_diag_flag")

hiv_data_logistic <- hiv_data_logistic %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # adjust reference levels as needed for interpretation:
    hiv_exposure_risk_group = as.factor(hiv_exposure_risk_group),
    sex                     = as.factor(sex),
    au_birth                = as.factor(au_birth),
    age_group               = as.factor(age_group),
    late_hiv_diag_flag      = as.factor(late_hiv_diag_flag)
    # Example: set ref levels explicitly (uncomment and edit):
    # hiv_exposure_risk_group = forcats::fct_relevel(hiv_exposure_risk_group, "MSM"),
    # sex                     = forcats::fct_relevel(sex, "Male"),
    # au_birth                = forcats::fct_relevel(au_birth, "Australia-born"),
    # age_group               = forcats::fct_relevel(age_group, "15-24"),
    # late_hiv_diag_flag      = forcats::fct_relevel(late_hiv_diag_flag, "0")
  )

# ---- 2) Assemble model frame and drop incomplete rows explicitly ----
mf <- hiv_data_logistic %>%
  dplyr::select(avg_travel_min_group_s100, dplyr::all_of(preds)) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na()

# ---- 3) Fit polr ----
model <- MASS::polr(
  avg_travel_min_group_s100 ~ hiv_exposure_risk_group + sex + au_birth + age_group + late_hiv_diag_flag,
  data = mf,
  Hess = TRUE
)

# ---- 4) Extract slope terms only (exclude thresholds/cutpoints with '|') ----
sumry <- summary(model)
coef_mat <- sumry$coefficients
all_terms <- rownames(coef_mat)
slope_keep <- !grepl("\\|", all_terms)   # TRUE for predictor coefficients
beta <- coef_mat[slope_keep, "Value"]
se   <- coef_mat[slope_keep, "Std. Error"]
tval <- coef_mat[slope_keep, "t value"]
term_names <- all_terms[slope_keep]

# ---- 5) Wald ORs, 95% CIs, p-values ----
OR   <- exp(beta)
LCL  <- exp(beta - 1.96 * se)
UCL  <- exp(beta + 1.96 * se)
pval <- 2 * pnorm(abs(tval), lower.tail = FALSE)

# ---- 6) Make terms human-readable: factor levels => "var:level" ----
readable_terms <- (function(nms) {
  # polr usually encodes factor levels as varLevel (e.g., sexFemale) or varB, etc.
  # Try to split at the first uppercase/level boundary for readability.
  # Fallback to original names if parsing fails.
  parsed <- vapply(nms, function(x) {
    # Try split by the first factor variable name present in the formula
    # If name contains a factor-style "varLevel", insert ":" before level.
    hit <- FALSE
    for (v in preds) {
      if (startsWith(x, v)) {
        lvl <- sub(paste0("^", v), "", x)
        # remove possible backticks
        lvl <- gsub("`", "", lvl)
        res <- if (nzchar(lvl)) paste0(v, ":", lvl) else v
        hit <- TRUE
        return(res)
      }
    }
    if (!hit) x else x
  }, character(1))
  unname(parsed)
})(term_names)

# ---- 7) Tidy result table ----
mv_or <- tibble::tibble(
  term    = readable_terms,
  OR      = as.numeric(OR),
  `2.5 %` = as.numeric(LCL),
  `97.5 %`= as.numeric(UCL),
  p_value = as.numeric(pval)
)

# ---- 8) Add simple model diagnostics ----
diag_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  n_used = nrow(mf),
  AIC    = AIC(model),
  df_resid = model$edf  # effective df for polr
)

print(mv_or)
print(diag_tbl)
```
